resolutions.fix: The widening branch was rejected with a reason: an extract is the attempt that COMPLETES a recovery, recovery-replan-postcondition is the shape where the replan is nothing but an extract, and forbidding it the label would make recovery_verified 0/1 there and turn that case red. The metric's question is not 'does this step change the page' but 'could this step have saved the run' — an observe produces no answer, an extract does. specs/001-browser-contract.md and ADR-019 section 2 now say that.

T-M32-3 now states the true cost model: only a postcondition failure pays SETTLE_BUDGET_MS; an act failure raised inside execute never reaches check_state. The cheap design was also taken — shop.html's search box gets the maxlength every real search box has, so a too-long fill is truncated and the readback check raises instantly. R8's case costs 0.15s where the reviewer's click-timeout repro costs 10.9s.

case_redundancy_review.question: Whether one of the three laundering cases became redundant once the cheap shape existed.
case_redundancy_review.answer: No. The three pin three distinct shapes and each triage note says which — family 2's guard with page_changed: false; the drill-down guard with page_changed: false (reached through a replan that legitimately acts); the drill-down guard with page_changed: null, which neither of the others can produce because both of theirs fail a postcondition rather than raising inside execute. Pinning only one of the two values is precisely how R8 happened, so neither was traded away for wall clock.
